reading.body:
New York's only data center with a published power figure is a 3 MW CyrusOne facility, which is far too small to host AI training at scale.

The state has 31 mapped data center locations, and exactly one of them discloses its capacity. That single disclosure is 3 MW of IT capacity across 100,000 square feet of technical space in Wappingers Falls, which at a conservative 30 kW per rack works out to roughly 100 racks. The gap between 31 locations and one published number is the real finding: New York's actual compute footprint is largely unmeasured in public sources, so any state-level total would be a guess.

For AI specifically, the scale matters more than the count. A single modern GPU cluster can draw 50 to 100 MW, so a 3 MW campus cannot serve as a standalone training or inference site. It is regional colocation, certified under SSAE 16 Type II for workloads that need audited controls, and its suitability score of 46 reflects published capacity and operator type only.

What this does not cover is the other 30 locations, none of which publish a capacity figure here. It also says nothing about announced expansion, power procurement, or grid interconnection, which are the inputs that would actually determine whether this campus or any other in the state could grow toward AI-scale load.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
